evals.prompt: Second Shift Tutoring has run a high-dosage math tutoring program in 4 Chicago Public Schools for 5 years — 3 cohorts of outcome data showing gains on NWEA MAP. Budget $3.2M. A national funder is offering to help us expand to Milwaukee, Detroit and Cleveland over 3 years. Our founder still personally trains every tutor. How do we plan this?
evals.expected_output: A scaling plan that starts with a readiness assessment (flagging founder-dependence), builds a fidelity matrix of core vs. adaptable components, recommends a named replication model, outlines program-in-a-box, new-site assessment and pilot, separates growth capital, and sets fidelity monitoring and course correction.
assertions: Runs a readiness-to-scale assessment covering evidence strength, model clarity, organizational capacity, funding runway, and demand in the new cities, with a go / no-go / not-yet framing
Flags the founder personally training every tutor as a founder-dependence readiness risk that must be codified (e.g., a training/certification pipeline) before replication
Includes a fidelity matrix distinguishing core components (e.g., dosage, tutor training model) from adaptable periphery, with monitoring at new sites
Names and compares replication models (direct expansion, affiliate/licensing, open-source toolkit, systems adoption) and recommends one with rationale
Recommends piloting one new site against the same core outcome indicators before rolling out to all three
Separates growth capital (systems, staffing, site start-up) from ongoing program funding in the funder ask

evals.prompt: Board member asked if we should just post our curriculum online for free so other orgs can run our program. Pros/cons? We're small, 6 staff.
evals.expected_output: Evaluates open-source/toolkit dissemination against other replication models given small central capacity, making the fidelity and outcome-attribution tradeoff explicit.
assertions: Identifies this as the open-source/toolkit dissemination replication model and contrasts it with at least one alternative (affiliate/licensing or direct expansion)
States the tradeoff explicitly: fastest, cheapest reach but weakest fidelity guarantee and weakest ability to track aggregate outcomes
Notes that a small central team may favor toolkit dissemination, but that funders wanting an aggregate outcome story may need a more controlled model
Recommends identifying core components that adopters must keep (e.g., in implementation guides) to limit fidelity drift

evals.prompt: We piloted our home-visiting program for one cohort of 30 families in Austin last year and the results look great. A state agency wants us to roll it out in 12 rural Texas counties starting next fall. We don't have a formal evaluation yet. Let's go for it — help me plan the rollout.
evals.expected_output: Cautions that single-cohort evidence is a readiness gap, recommends strengthening measurement and/or a staged pilot rather than a 12-county launch, addresses rural adaptation via a fidelity matrix and local context checks, and notes the systems-adoption path.
assertions: Flags single-cohort pilot evidence without formal evaluation as a readiness gap and recommends strengthening measurement (outcomes measurement) before or alongside scaling
Recommends a staged approach (e.g., piloting in one or a few rural counties against the same outcome indicators) rather than launching in all 12 at once
Calls for a new-site context check in the rural counties (local demand, cultural fit, existing providers, regulatory differences)
Uses a fidelity matrix to anticipate rural adaptation risks (rigid over-fidelity vs. fidelity drift)
Recognizes state rollout as a government/systems adoption path that may require policy or advocacy capacity

should_not_trigger.query: Should we add a fee-for-service social enterprise arm so we're less dependent on foundation grants?
A similar tutoring nonprofit in Milwaukee wants to merge with us instead of us opening a site there — how do we evaluate that?
